docs.title: SOC Analyst Lab Portfolio & Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to my cybersecurity lab notebook. This portfolio documents hands-on defensive security simulations, alert triage, threat-hunting scenarios, and log analysis performed across virtual and cloud environments.

docs.title: 🎯 Focus Areas
docs.text:
• Security Operations & Alert Triage: Analyzing endpoint and network telemetry to determine True/False positives.
  • Log Correlation & Detection: Writing and tuning detection queries using SPL and KQL.
  • Threat Hunting & Forensics: Investigating packet captures (PCAPs), process trees, and persistence artifacts.
  • Defensive Frameworks: Mapping adversary tactics directly to the MITRE ATT&CK matrix.

docs.title: Lab 01: Windows Telemetry & Process Creation Auditing (Event ID 4688)
docs.text:
• Date: October 2026
  • Category: Endpoint Telemetry & Incident Analysis
  • Framework Mapping: MITRE ATT&CK [T1059 - Command and Scripting Interpreter] / [T1082 - System Information Discovery]
  • Target OS: Windows 10/11 Enterprise

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Objective
docs.text:
Adversaries routinely execute native binaries (Living off the Land) to enumerate accounts, query network configurations, and spawn malicious payloads. By default, Windows does not log granular process execution data.

The objective of this lab was to configure Audit Process Creation within the Local Security Policy, generate process execution telemetry, and analyze the resulting Event ID 4688 forensic artifacts to understand parent-child process relationships.

docs.title: 2. Methodology & Configuration
docs.text:
1. Auditing Policy Configuration:
  2. Navigated to Advanced Audit Policy Configuration > System Audit Policies > Detailed Tracking.
  3. Enabled Audit Process Creation for both Success and Failure.
  4. Log Acquisition:
  5. Monitored the Security event log via Windows Event Viewer (eventvwr.msc).
  6. Filtered telemetry using event filter EventID == 4688.

docs.title: Telemetry Overview: Filtered Security Event Stream
Key Artifact Breakdown:
docs.text:
• Event ID: 4688 (A new process has been created)
  • Account / Security ID: SYSTEM (Authority/System-level context)
  • New Process Name: C:\Windows\System32\svchost.exe (The spawned binary)
  • Creator (Parent) Process Name: C:\Windows\System32\services.exe (The launching binary)
  • Mandatory Label: System Mandatory Level (High integrity execution token)

docs.title: Analytical Insight:
docs.text: In a typical enterprise SOC environment, mapping the Parent Process (Creator Process Name) to the Child Process (New Process Name) establishes the process lineage. While services.exe spawning svchost.exe represents expected baseline activity, an anomalous parent (such as winword.exe spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe) would represent a high-confidence indicator of compromise (IOC) indicative of macro exploitation.

docs.title: 4. Defensive Takeaways for SOC Triage
docs.text:
• Baseline Profiling: Knowing what should launch a process is just as important as knowing what the binary does. Legitimate system binaries executing under abnormal parents must be flagged immediately.
  • Log Enrichment: Standard 4688 logging provides binary names, but enabling the sub-setting "Include command line in process creation events" adds the full CLI arguments, essential for identifying obfuscated scripts (e.g., base64-encoded PowerShell).

docs.title: Lab 02: Network Traffic Analysis & Cleartext HTTP Stream Reconstruction
docs.text:
• Date: October 2026
  • Category: Network Security & Packet Forensics
  • Framework Mapping: MITRE ATT&CK [T1071.001 - Web Protocols] / [TA0011 - Command and Control]
  • Tooling: Wireshark, Protocol Hierarchy, TCP Stream Analysis

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Objective
docs.text:
Network telemetry provides an objective source of truth during defensive triage, exposing external communications even if endpoint logs are absent or purged.

The objective of this lab was to triage a packet capture (.cap), identify active layer-3 and layer-4 conversations across modern IPv6 infrastructure, isolate unencrypted application-layer requests, and reconstruct the full bidirectional TCP session to extract key forensic indicators.

docs.title: 2. Triage Methodology
docs.text:
1. Endpoint & Protocol Enumeration:
  2. Evaluated the global protocol distribution using Wireshark Protocol Hierarchy.
  3. Identified active communication channels via the IPv6 Endpoints table.
  4. Display Filter Application:
  5. Applied the display filter http.request to isolate client-initiated web requests from transport-layer overhead.
  6. Layer 7 Stream Reconstruction:
  7. Reconstructed the complete conversational flow using Follow TCP Stream to inspect request headers and server responses.

docs.title: Telemetry Overview: HTTP Request Frame Isolation
Key Artifact Breakdown:
docs.text:
• Frame ID: 49
  • Protocol: HTTP/1.0
  • Source IP (Client): 2001:6f8:102d:0:2d0:9ff:fee3:e8de
  • Destination IP (Host): 2001:6f8:900:7c0::2
  • Destination Port: 80 (Standard HTTP)
  • Source Port: 59201 (Ephemeral Client Port)
  • Host Header: cl-1985.ham-01.de.sixxs.net
  • User-Agent: Lynx/2.8.6rel.2 libwww-FM/2.14 SSL-MM/1.4.1 OpenSSL/0.9.8b
  • Response Code: HTTP/1.1 200 OK (Apache Web Server)

docs.title: Analytical Insight:
docs.text:
• Cleartext Visibility: Because the transaction occurred over unencrypted HTTP (port 80), all request headers, user agents, and response payloads are exposed.
  • Client Fingerprinting: The User-Agent string identifies a terminal-based web browser (Lynx), rather than a standard GUI browser like Chrome or Edge. In an enterprise environment, non-standard user agents originating from end-user workstations warrant immediate investigation as potential script execution or automated tooling.
  • Content Inspection: The server returned an open directory listing exposing downloadable files (.pdf, .htm). In a real incident scenario, any retrieved binaries would be carved via File > Export Objects > HTTP and submitted for hash analysis.

docs.title: 4. Defensive Takeaways for SOC Triage
docs.text:
• Network Baselines: Modern enterprise web communications are overwhelmingly encrypted via TLS (port 443). Outbound cleartext HTTP (port 80) should be monitored and flagged for inspection.
  • Full-Session Context: Individual packet inspection shows fragmented data; following the TCP stream reconstructs the entire conversational context needed for defensible incident reporting.
